title: Accessibility
summary: How contrast is promised. This pack does not measure contrast.

questions.prompt: Is contrast guaranteed by the scale, or checked afterwards?
questions.summary: Pick when the contrast promise is made.

options.label: Guaranteed by the scale
options.summary: The scale itself promises the contrast.
options.why: The scale itself promises contrast, so you do not run a separate check later.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if every step must meet contrast by construction.
options.formula: Contrast is a property of the scale, not a later test.

options.label: Checked afterwards
options.summary: A person checks contrast after values exist.
options.why: You pick the scale first, and a person checks contrast once the values exist.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if contrast is a review step, not a scale rule.
trade_offs: A good-looking scale can fail the review
options.formula: Contrast is reviewed after the values are written.

questions.why_care: It decides whether contrast is built into the color steps or reviewed once the values exist.

questions.prompt: How large is a touch target beyond the floor?
questions.summary: The floor is 24 px. Material recommends 48 px at every density.
questions.why_care: It keeps the 24 px floor and records the 48 px recommendation.

options.label: 48 px recommendation
options.summary: Material asks for 48 px targets at every density.
options.why: Material says every touch target should be at least 48 px, at any density. The WCAG floor stays 24 px.
options.when_to_choose: Choose this if you follow Material's 48 px target on top of the floor.
trade_offs: Dense screens give up a little space.

sources.name: Material
sources.title: Using Material density on the web
sources.quote: No matter the density, all touch targets should be at least 48px in size.
